before: Existing pure planners consumed native text and resolved format ranges. No shared compiler exposed parsed inline text, semantic marks, distinct hyperlink owners, and complete opaque atoms for composition.
after: A bounded pure compiler returns detached immutable inline tokens, link paths/targets/titles, complete inert atoms, and the full input AST. Plain text is unavailable until atom ownership is resolved.
reason: The compiler creates no canonical nodes, native IDs, relationships, live writes, or shared state. D15 retains native mapping and complete-target planner composition. Unknown inline data and expressions remain inert. No collaboration, payload, journal, or document format changes.
